content.title: All About Cameron and Cayden Boozer's 2 Siblings, Brother Carmani and Sister Bloom
content.text: NEED TO KNOW Cameron and Cayden Boozer were born to parents Carlos and CeCe Boozer on July 18, 2007They have an older brother, Carmani, and a younger sister, BloomThe twins were born via in vitro fertilization, in part, to help save Carmani's life Cameron and Cayden Boozer are some of basketball’s brightest rising stars, but they’re far from the only athletes in their family. The twins — who both play for the Duke Blue Devils — were born to parents Carlos, a former NBA star, and CeCe Boozer, a former Division I volleyball player, in 2007. They have an older brother, Carmani Boozer, who plays baseball. Four years after his 2015 divorce from CeCe, Carlos welcomed a daughter named Bloom with his second wife, Aneshka Smith, in 2019. The two have since divorced. Cameron and Cayden's story is closely linked with their older brother's. Shortly after his birth in 2006, Carmani was diagnosed with sickle cell anemia, an inherited blood disorder. After researching the disease, the parents learned that Carmani’s best chance at a cure was a bone marrow transplant using stem cells from the umbilical cord of a sibling. The twins were born via in vitro fertilization in 2007. "You go through the tough times and when things start to get sweet, they're that much sweeter," Carlos told Deseret News in April 2008, nearly a year after Carmani's transplant, which was successful. "It's so much fun right now. My whole family is back together." Here’s everything to know about Cameron and Cayden Boozer’s siblings, including older brother Carmani and younger sister Bloom. Carmani was diagnosed with sickle cell anemia as a newborn Carlos and Carmani Boozer in October 2025. Carlos Boozer/Instagram The oldest child in the Boozer family developed sickle cell anemia at a young age, first starting to develop symptoms shortly after his birth on May 31, 2006, per ESPN. According to the Cleveland Clinic, sickle cell is an inherited blood disorder that can cause symptoms such as “fatigue from anemia, infections and severe pain.” Both Carlos and CeCe were carriers for the sickle cell trait, which is present in around one in 12 African American people, per ESPN. When both parents have the trait, it’s more likely that their children will develop symptoms. At the time he was diagnosed, the Boozers were told that there was “no known cure,” which sparked a search for answers from CeCe. The twins were born, in part, to help save Carmani’s life Carlos, CeCe, Carmani, Cameron and Cayden Boozer. Carlos Boozer/Instagram While researching answers, CeCe learned that her son's best chance at a cure was a bone marrow transplant using stem cells from the umbilical cord of a sibling. Inspired by the revelation, CeCe and Carlos found a team of doctors to help conceive a sibling for Carmani via in vitro fertilization. To prevent a sibling from also being born with sickle cell anemia, the doctors conducted extensive testing on the embryos. Twenty-six eggs were fertilized, 10 were genetically compatible and two were sickle cell-free, per ESPN. Both embryos were implanted, and within weeks, the couple were expecting twins. Cameron and Cayden were born on July 18, 2007. Related Stories After they were born, Carmani underwent two rounds of chemotherapy to make his body more likely to accept his brothers' transplanted stem cells. The transplant — which required a 40-day stay in the hospital — was ultimately deemed a success, and Carmani was declared cured of sickle cell anemia in May 2008. Speaking about their bond, Carmani told ESPN2 in the 2024 documentary Blood Brothers that their childhood “brought them together more than anything,” adding, “They saved my life.” Carmani plays college baseball at the University of Fort Lauderdale The Boozer family. Carlos Boozer/Instagram These days, Carmani attends the University of Fort Lauderdale in Florida, where he plays on the baseball team, per his bio. It’s not the only sport that Carmani plays, though. The oldest Boozer child has also joined his dad on the golf course over the years. Bloom was born in 2019 Carlos and Bloom Boozer. Carlos Boozer/Instagram Seven years after Carlos and CeCe married in 2002, Carlos filed for divorce. Their divorce was finalized in 2015. Carlos went on to marry Smith in June 2017, per Ebony. The two welcomed their daughter, Bloom Boheme Boozer, on April 5, 2019. "Introducing Bloom Boheme Boozer!!!! At 37 Years Old, I Didn’t Know I Could Fall In Love All Over Again... Then Came Bloom... My Beautiful Wife Gave Me Our Gorgeous Angel!!! Filled With So Many Emotions!!!" Carlos wrote on Instagram at the time. "The Journey For @bloomboheme Being With Us Is A Story Best Told By Her Mom, But Just Know When I Call Her A Blessing, She Is Exactly That!!! And Fellas, She’s Got 3 BEASTY Brothers & One Bad Ass Father To Get Through Before Ya’ll Get A Date!!! FACTS 🤣!!!" Carlos and Smith have since divorced. Bloom is close with her father and brothers Cameron and Cayden Boozer with their family in December 2024. Carlos Boozer/Instagram From a young age, Bloom has been close to her dad. In June 2020, Smith noted the strong bond between father and daughter in a Father’s Day post on Instagram, writing that they “have the most beautiful bond.” “The way she lights up seeing her dad makes me kind of jealous sometimes not all the time lol. I know we are truly meant to be her parents, navigating and guiding her journey towards being her highest self,” she wrote in the caption. Carlos frequently shares insight into his youngest child’s life on Instagram, sharing photos and videos documenting their adventures. In April 2024, the family went to Disney for Bloom's 5th birthday. "Anything For You Baby Girl…" he captioned a video montage on Instagram. She loves her older brothers, too. In February 2020, Bloom's Instagram account — which is run by her parents — posted a photo of Cayden cradling his baby sister. "Cayden and I 🥰 👨‍👧," the caption reads.
